messages:
Ashley: quick question — i'm sketching a lighter-weight handshake for dynamic cohort ownership in the continuous batcher. goal: avoid long synchronous rebalances while keeping KV-cache locality and headroom signals accurate. thoughts?

Miguel: curious to see the sketch. are you thinking leases or tokens?

Ashley: lease tokens. cheap ttl-based claim + a small renewal window. basic flow: acquire lease -> start accepting requests for cohort -> emit headroom telemetry -> renew periodically. if renew fails, gracefully drain and transfer. pseudo: 
```
lease = lease_acquire(cohort_id, owner_id, ttl_ms=250)
if lease.ok: accept()
else: fallback_to_microqueue()
```
Need help on corner cases around hot reassigns.

Kim: two quick concerns: 1) what happens to in-flight KV cache entries if ownership flips mid-token? 2) how do we avoid thundering renewals when many workers race to claim?

Ashley: good calls. for KV we planned soft-eviction: owner marks cache as handoff_in_progress, continues serving cached gets for a short grace (50ms), and advertises reduced headroom so others avoid packing. for renewals we jitter + exponential backoff on failures, and randomize renew windows.

Sajal: what about fairness? high-throughput tenants could hog a cohort lease forever and starve small requests. any admission shape?

Ashley: yes — leases carry a credit budget tied to observed token consumption. when budget exhausted, owner either extends with slowdown policies or releases early. credits are replenished slowly to prevent noisy bursts gaming churn.

Miguel: can we piggyback on existing slot-credit ledger? reusing telemetry would reduce infra churn. also emit an explicit reason when lease is released (evict, budget, heartbeat timeout) for postmortem traces.

InfraBot: scheduled job: lease-lease-audit-run every 5m. will collect lease_state, owner_id, last_renew_ts, eviction_reason.

Nina: small nit — the cache handoff grace needs to be proportional to request p95 compute of the model. 50ms might be too small for longer sequences. suggest: grace = max(50ms, p95_latency * 1.2).

Ashley: agreed. i'll parameterize that. also thinking of fallback: if lease_acquire fails, route to micro-queue with very low packing (fastpath) instead of slow single-tenant queue. keeps latency SLOs for small requests.

Devon: how do we detect lease thrashing? if leases flip frequently we can lose KV locality and spike tail latency. need metric: lease_flip_rate per cohort and a circuit breaker to pin owner for at least N leases or M seconds.

Sajal: +1 circuit breaker. maybe add a cool-down that forces incoming claimers to wait a random backoff if flip_rate > threshold. also track cumulative cost of flips to decide if we should trigger a manual reassignment.

Kim: edge case: what if owner fails but doesn't release (network partition)? others shouldn't accept until TTL expires or explicit forced takeover. worried about split-brain accepting concurrent writes to cache.

Ashley: TTL-based resolution is simpler and safer. to mitigate window we keep cache writes idempotent and versioned, plus owners write a short-lived owner_manifest in shared metadata store so takeover checks manifest_version before accepting. takeover path logs the collision for later analysis.

Miguel: we should prototype with two cohorts: small-window (fast path, no KV reliance) and large-cohort (lease + cache). run A/B on a subset of tenants and capture these metrics: lease_flip_rate, headroom_miss_rate, tail_latency_p99, cache_hit_rate, takeover_count.

Nina: agree on metrics. also capture the handoff grace expiration counts — how often handoff runs out and causes full cold-cache misses.

Ashley: next steps: i'll draft an RFC with these primitives (lease token structure, credit budget rules, handoff grace config, circuit breaker heuristics) and add the prototype toggles + telemetry we discussed. aiming for a short-term experiment on canary fleet.

Devon: sounds good. if you want, i can add the circuit breaker implementation + unit tests.

Ashley: thanks! i'll ping a draft in #eng-runtime tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Miguel: one more ops thing — ensure eviction_reason is indexed in logs so SRE can create alerts on takeover spikes.

Ashley: noted. will include log schema.

InfraBot: reminder: deploy window tomorrow 08:00-09:00 UTC for canary changes.

Kim: ping me on the RFC; want to review the cache handoff invariants.

Ashley: will do. thanks everyone. :rocket:
